messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert — elevated KV cache growth + continuous-batching latency spike on us-east-1-primary. Error rate up for model=redwood-gemini-3, approximate tail p50->p95 shift detected. Auto-throttle did not engage.
Alice Chen: seeing it in dashboards, p95 token latency jumped to 1.8s, KV cache entries ballooning. paging Eng-Oncall. @Ben can you pick this up?
Ben Ortiz: on it. grabbing logs and current batch config. what customer impact?
Maya Rao: noticed 5 customer incidents opened — a few chat sessions timing out/failing to complete. CS pinged us.
Liam Park (CS): 3 paying customers reported streaming stalls, 1 observed truncated responses. They're asking for ETA.
Ben Ortiz: initial triage: speculative decoding + continuous batching + KV cache interaction seems to be generating large draft/target divergence, causing repeated KV entries per request. that increases memory and amplification across batching.
Ravi Patel: can we confirm whether speculative-decoder rollout from last night changed draft length heuristics? I pushed a conservative change in staging but not prod.
Ben Ortiz: prod config shows speculative.enabled=true and speculative.threshold=0.15 (we pushed that 02:41 UTC last night).
Alice Chen: ok, we need quick mitigation to stop cache blowup and reduce tail latency. Options: 1) temporarily disable speculative decoding; 2) tighten batching window; 3) enable KV eviction aggressive policy. Which is quickest?
Maya Rao: eviction will help but is slower to take effect; disabling speculative is fastest and safe. rolling disable + canary.
Ben Ortiz: agree. plan: push config change to set speculative.enabled=false for us-east-1-primary, disable oncanary=50% then 100% if stable. Also reduce max_batch_latency_ms from 50->20 for that pool to reduce batching amplification.
Alice Chen: @deploy-bot can you start the canary? tag: deploy/speculative-toggle/us-east-1-primary
deploy-bot: Deploy job queued — id dpl-20260717-4321. Canary to 10 hosts first. Estimated rollout 90s.
Ben Ortiz: patch to runtime config: ```yaml
speculative:
  enabled: false
  threshold: 0.15
batching:
  max_batch_latency_ms: 20
  max_batch_size: 32
kvcache:
  eviction_policy: aggressive
```
Ben Ortiz: applying now to canary.
Alice Chen: monitoring DPM and token backlog. set alerts if p95 improves by 30% within 3m.
Maya Rao: I'm watching customer queue; pinging CS with tentative mitigation and ETA 10m.
Liam Park (CS): relaying to customers: "We are rolling a targeted mitigation that should restore streaming within ~10 minutes; will update as we confirm."
Ben Ortiz: canary applied. logs: seeing immediate reduction in new KV insert rate. tail latency trending down.
Ben Ortiz: pushing to 100% now. deploy-bot: Canary ok, starting rollout to remaining hosts (approx 2m).
deploy-bot: Rollout complete.
Maya Rao: p95 dropped from 1.8s -> 0.6s within 90s of full rollout. error rate down 82%. customer queue decreasing.
Ravi Patel: good. we should capture root cause: speculative heuristic produced more draft divergence for long-context sessions causing repeated KV mismatches and cache key churn across batches. seems amplified by larger batching window.
Alice Chen: agreed. immediate postmortem actions: 1) revert speculative.threshold change in prod rollout notes; 2) add automated throttle if KV insert rate spikes > X per host; 3) add a canary gate for speculative toggles with perf guardrails.
Ben Ortiz: logging ticket #INC-2026-178 to track follow-ups and patch backport. I'll attach traces and a small repro harness.
Maya Rao: scheduling oncall handoff to night team — adding Ravi as secondary for follow-up.
Ravi Patel: I'll run a stress test against prod dev cluster with varied speculative thresholds to find safe default.
Liam Park (CS): customers updated: two said immediate improvement, third is still validating — will confirm in 30m.
Alice Chen: thanks everyone. keep thread for postmortem notes, assign owner for each action. I'll start the incident doc and tag Eng/ML for model heuristic review. :thumbsup:
Ben Ortiz: owner for runtime mitigations: Ben. I'll open PRs for auto-throttle and canary guard.
Maya Rao: SRE follow-ups: Maya — eviction policy tuning + alert thresholds.
Ravi Patel: ML follow-ups: Ravi — spec-decoder heuristics and rollout process.
incident-bot: Incident SEV2 -> resolved (mitigation applied). Duration 00:14:12.
Alice Chen: closing update: resolved, customers notified, will run postmortem tomorrow 15:00 UTC.
Liam Park (CS): thanks team, customers already sent thank-you notes for quick response.
